newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Euskaltel telecom approves capital increases.
newsitem.headline: Spain Euskaltel telecom approves capital increases.

text.p: Spain's Basque regional telephone operator Euskaltel said on Tuesday its shareholders had approved a capital increase of 7.78 billion pesetas.
A second capital increase of 6.02 billion pesetas to be carried out in the next two months was also approved at a shareholders meeting, the company said in a statement.

The first increase will be underwritten by the Basque government, savings banks Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa, Gipuzkoa Donostia Kutxa and Caja de Ahorros de Vitoria y Alava and public company Euskal Irrati Telebista.
The second increase will be underwritten by Retevision, Endesa, Italy's Stet and "other partners whose participation is currently under negotiation," the company said.

After the second increase, Euskaltel's shareholder base will comprise the following: BBK 23.5 percent; Kutxa 18.5 percent; Vital five percent; Vasco five percent; EITB five percent; Stet 18 percent; Endesa 10 percent; Retevision three percent; and others 12 percent.
Euskatel was formed in 1995 with the objective of becoming an overall telecoms operator in Spain's northern Basque region.
The Basque operator is part of the consortium which won the bid for 70 percent of Retevision, Spain's second basic telephone operator.
